newsitem.title: USA: Carter urges release of Russian journalists in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Carter urges release of Russian journalists in Chechnya.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter on Wednesday called for the release of three Russian journalists who were kidnapped in Chechnya over the weekend.

Television reporter Yelena Masyuk and two members of her crew from the Russian commercial network NTV were abducted by masked gunman on Saturday in the Chechen village of Samashki, 20 miles (32 km) west of the capital Grozny, a Carter Centre spokeswoman said.

Masyuk, known in Russia for her award-winning coverage of the Chechen conflict, was a media fellow at Duke University in 1995 under a programme sponsored by Carter's Commission on Radio and Television Policy, which is devoted to the development of democratic media principles worldwide.
"We at the Carter Centre are deeply concerned about her and her colleagues and urge their swift and safe release," the former president said in a statement.

"I met Yelena Masyuk when she visited the Carter Centre in 1995. I have been impressed with her professionalism and heroic dedication to reporting news from Chechnya despite difficult conditions there," he said.
According to the Carter Centre, the abduction of the NTV crew brought to seven the number of journalists held by kidnappers in the republic.
Moscow dispatched tens of thousands of soldiers to Chechnya in 1994 to crush a drive for independence from the Russian Federation.
Despite a ceasefire in August and the withdrawal of Russian troops, the largely Moslem region continues to be awash with weaponry, maverick rebels, armed bandits and kidnap gangs.
